findings.summary: The new condition is correct for every value the data model can produce. List and card stay in sync for all non-negative integers.
findings.evidence: Student.ticketBalance is number (src/types/index.ts:12). GAS integer_(r[6], ..., 0) rejects any value that is not a safe integer or is below 0 (gas/Code.gs:610-612, 628), so the sheet cannot supply negative or fractional balances. The demo API validates initial balances (api.ts:363) and blocks completion when the balance is short (api.ts:408). The list now treats 0 as red and 1-2 as amber; the card counts <=2. Those sets are the same. The only path to an out-of-range value is hand-edited demo localStorage, which getStored (api.ts:119-133) does not validate. In that case a negative balance would be counted by the card but shown green in the list.
findings.suggestedFix: None required. Optionally write isZero as ticketBalance <= 0 for defence in depth.

findings.summary: The useState wrapper is safe and restored in finally. It depends on the tab initializer's return values, but drift would make the test fail rather than pass falsely.
findings.evidence: Only one useState in TeacherDashboard has a lazy initializer returning 'today' or 'allRides' (line 66). The other lazy initializer (line 69) returns a date string. The wrapper calls each lazy initializer one extra time, which is harmless because they have no side effects. The TSX is transpiled to CommonJS, so useState resolves as react_1.useState at call time and the patch takes effect. If the initializer changes, LOWUI-01 fails because the students heading would be missing. LOWUI-05 renders the 'today' tab from the same fixture and compares the card count with the number of amber or red list badges, which ties list and card together. My summary-card mutants confirm this check catches a mismatch.
